Hi, I made this. OpenVids is a desktop video editor where you describe what you want in chat and agents edit the timeline. A director agent splits the work between specialists (editor, vision, motion design, audio, research), and you watch the timeline change while they work. It's still a normal editor underneath, so you can fix things by hand. It's a fork of HeyGen's HyperFrames. There's no account and no cloud: you bring your own API key and the project is a folder of files on your machine. All your video projects live in one place, instead of being scattered across messy chats in Claude Code or Codex. Two things I built because the first version was bad: - Agents kept saying "done" on videos with black frames or dead audio. ## What is OpenChatCut?

OpenChatCut is an open-source ChatCut alternative: a video editor that brings conversational agents and professional timeline editing into the same workspace. It is independent open source (AGPL), not affiliated with the commercial ChatCut product.

OpenChatCut = local video projects + multitrack timeline + AI agents + MCP + production-ready exports.

It does not merely generate a video that can no longer be changed. Every edit is written to real tracks, clips, transitions, captions, effects, and media inside the project. You can continue editing manually, undo or redo changes, save versions, or hand the project to another agent. [...] Website: 
 Open-source ChatCut alternative guide: 
 ChatCut vs OpenChatCut: 
 🤖 Agent-native: the built-in agent and external MCP agents share the same editing tools.
 🎞️ Real timeline: multiple video and audio tracks, transitions, effects, LUTs, zooms, and keyframes.
 📝 Transcript-driven editing: word-level transcription, text-based cuts, pause handling, speakers, and linked captions.
 ✨ Generation and media: images, video, speech, music, sound effects, and online media search.
 🧩 Motion Graphics and WebGL: editable motion templates, custom shaders, visual effects, and transitions.

results.title: AI Agent Video Editors: The MCP Takeover | Zentor Blog
results.content:
What is ChatCut and how does the Codex plugin work?

ChatCut is a full closed-source AI video editor whose timeline is reachable through a hosted interface. Its Codex plugin, which opened access on July 9, 2026, lets you edit from a Codex chat by describing what you want. Every edit returns as an editable timeline, with MP4 or XML export back to Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Is there an open-source alternative to ChatCut?

Yes, with trade-offs. OpenCut is an open-source CapCut alternative with a large following, but its agent and MCP layer is still on the roadmap. Palmier Pro is open-source under GPLv3 with an MCP server live today, but it runs only on macOS 26 and Apple Silicon. ChatCut itself is closed, and its plugin repository carries no license. [...] References ChatCut ChatGPT/Codex Plugin  ·  ChatCut on Product Hunt  ·  ChatCut Launches Codex Plugin (MarTech Series)  ·  ChatCut agent-plugin (GitHub)  ·  OpenCut: The open-source CapCut alternative (GitHub)  ·  Palmier Pro: The video editor built for AI  ·  Palmier Pro (GitHub)  ·  Model Context Protocol [...] The catch is ownership. You need a ChatCut account, and the public agent-plugin repository carries no license and only a few hundred stars. This path suits the editor who says "I am not switching editors, I just want to point an agent at the one I have."

### OpenCut: rewrite an open-source editor from scratch

OpenCut is the open-source CapCut alternative, one of the most-starred editors on GitHub (north of 45,000 stars) with backing that includes Vercel and fal.ai. It has the most thorough rewrite plan of the three: an Editor API, an MCP server, headless batch rendering, and a Rust core meant to run across web, desktop, and mobile from one codebase.
